joe-biden.title: Joe Biden
joe-biden.body:
## Ghostwriter tapes (2026)

Recordings of Joe Biden speaking with his memoir ghostwriter [[mark-zwonitzer|Mark Zwonitzer]] were released in July 2026 after a lengthy legal fight, capturing Biden warning at one point that "some of this may be classified" and later stating, "this is classified."[{n}] The more than seventy hours of 2016 and 2017 conversations had been obtained during special counsel [[robert-hur|Robert Hur]]'s classified documents probe and were published by the [[oversight-project|Oversight Project]]; Biden's attorneys spent months trying to block the release before abandoning their lawsuit, and a judge accepted the dismissal on the Monday preceding the report.[{n}]

In one exchange Biden tells Zwonitzer: "Some of this may be classified … So, be careful. I'm not sure … It's not marked classified but —." At another point he says, "The next thing I have here is, um, this is classified …"[{n}] The tapes also show Biden frequently pausing, speaking haltingly and struggling to recall events, details that align with Hur's earlier description of Biden's memory.[{n}] Oversight Project Vice President of Litigation [[jeff-clark|Jeff Clark]] said the recordings should force a full reexamination of the decision to give Biden a pass for keeping and disclosing classified information.[{n}]

mark-zwonitzer.title: Mark Zwonitzer
mark-zwonitzer.body:
Mark Zwonitzer is the ghostwriter who worked with [[joe-biden|Joe Biden]] on his memoir and whose recorded 2016 and 2017 conversations with Biden became evidence in special counsel [[robert-hur|Robert Hur]]'s classified documents investigation.[{n}]

## The tapes

More than seventy hours of Zwonitzer's recorded interviews were published by the [[oversight-project|Oversight Project]] in July 2026 after Biden's attorneys abandoned a months-long effort to block their release.[{n}] On the tapes Biden warns Zwonitzer, "Some of this may be classified … So, be careful. I'm not sure … It's not marked classified but —," and elsewhere states, "The next thing I have here is, um, this is classified …"[{n}] The recordings also capture Biden pausing frequently, speaking haltingly and struggling to recall events.[{n}]

robert-hur.title: Robert Hur
robert-hur.body:
## Biden classified documents probe

Robert Hur is the special counsel whose classified documents investigation obtained more than seventy hours of recordings of [[joe-biden|Joe Biden]] speaking with ghostwriter [[mark-zwonitzer|Mark Zwonitzer]] in 2016 and 2017.[{n}] When the [[oversight-project|Oversight Project]] published the tapes in July 2026, reporting noted that Biden's frequent pauses, halting speech and difficulty recalling events aligned with Hur's earlier description of Biden's memory.[{n}] Oversight Project litigation chief [[jeff-clark|Jeff Clark]] said the recordings should force a full reexamination of the decision to give Biden a pass for keeping and disclosing classified information.[{n}]

jeff-clark.title: Jeff Clark
jeff-clark.body:
## Oversight Project role

Jeff Clark served as Vice President of Litigation at the [[oversight-project|Oversight Project]] when the organization published more than seventy hours of recordings of [[joe-biden|Joe Biden]] speaking with his memoir ghostwriter [[mark-zwonitzer|Mark Zwonitzer]] in July 2026.[{n}] Clark said the recordings should force a full reexamination of the decision to give Biden a pass for keeping and disclosing classified information, a decision that followed special counsel [[robert-hur|Robert Hur]]'s investigation.[{n}]

openai.title: OpenAI
openai.body:
## Open-source AI dispute (2026)

OpenAI, led by [[sam-altman|Sam Altman]], was grouped with [[anthropic|Anthropic]] in July 2026 as a company that has generally supported stronger safeguards for frontier AI systems, in contrast to advocates of [[open-source-artificial-intelligence|open-source AI]] who argue that excessive regulation would entrench incumbent firms and reduce America's ability to compete globally.[{n}] Venture capitalist [[chamath-palihapitiya|Chamath Palihapitiya]] warned that a government ban on open-source AI would tank the market and crater both OpenAI and Anthropic.[{n}]

[[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] argued that the push by Altman and [[dario-amodei|Dario Amodei]] for government regulation was an attempt to slow and control the industry's acceleration rather than supercharge an American Age of Abundance, and cited former White House AI and Crypto Czar [[david-sacks|David Sacks]] as openly stating that the two companies seek regulation in order to stave off competitors.[{n}]

sam-altman.title: Sam Altman
sam-altman.body:
## Regulation push and the AI shadow war

[[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] argued in July 2026 that the concerted effort by Sam Altman of [[openai|OpenAI]] and [[dario-amodei|Dario Amodei]] of [[anthropic|Anthropic]] to seek government regulation for the nascent, rapidly-accelerating AI industry was not an attempt to supercharge the American push into an Age of Abundance but to slow and control that push, putting it "in collectivist, oligarchic hands."[{n}] In that framing, Altman and Amodei revealed themselves "not as accelerants to the AI agenda, but retardants to it."[{n}] Former White House AI and Crypto Czar [[david-sacks|David Sacks]] made a parallel argument, stating that the two companies seek regulation to stave off competitors — a position at odds with the administration's stated aim, voiced by Commerce Secretary [[howard-lutnick|Howard Lutnick]], of protecting [[open-source-artificial-intelligence|open source AI]].[{n}]

howard-lutnick.title: Howard Lutnick
howard-lutnick.body:
## Open-source AI (2026)

White House Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick — described by [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] as "the core voice behind Trump's Tariff Trade Agenda" — reportedly said in late July 2026 that the administration aims to "protect open source AI."[{n}] The statement was cited as one of three weekend indicators, alongside remarks by former AI and Crypto Czar [[david-sacks|David Sacks]] and China's timed open-weight model releases, that the [[open-source-artificial-intelligence|open-source AI]] shadow war was breaking in favor of acceleration rather than the regulatory approach urged by [[openai|OpenAI]] and [[anthropic|Anthropic]].[{n}]

china.title: China
china.body:
## Open-source AI strategy (2026)

In the July 2026 dispute over [[open-source-artificial-intelligence|open-source artificial intelligence]], Trump-aligned technologists argued that restricting open-source AI development would weaken US competitiveness while benefiting foreign rivals, particularly China.[{n}] [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] went further, writing that China was "continuing to rug-pull the closed-source and closed-weight American AI industry by timing strategic releases of open-source and open-weight models" that simultaneously accelerate the industry as a whole while blunting Western attempts to slow it down.[{n}] On his account, these releases grant President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] the narrative shielding required to resist the regulation push and continue the acceleration path — meaning China is "actually HELPING protect the future of an open-source, open-weight, FREE AI world" while the biggest voices in the American AI industry try to get Western governments to stop it.[{n}] He concluded: "Good thing Trump and [[xi-jinping|Xi]] are Sovereign Bros."[{n}]

xi-jinping.title: Xi Jinping
xi-jinping.body:
## "Sovereign Bros" framing

Concluding his July 2026 analysis of the [[open-source-artificial-intelligence|open-source AI]] shadow war, [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] wrote that [[china|China]]'s timed releases of open-weight AI models were protecting a free AI future and giving President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] the narrative cover to resist domestic regulation, adding: "Good thing Trump and Xi are Sovereign Bros."[{n}]
